data-center-operators-and-cloud-buyers-p.text: Data Center Operators & Cloud Buyers - Proof of Deployable AI Capacity | Journo Request Sourcee Open main menu Features Pricing Reviews FAQ Log in Start free trial Posted in last 7 days Data Center Operators & Cloud Buyers - Proof of Deployable AI Capacity We are announcing AI capacity faster than we can make it real. A GPU commitment is not deployable capacity. Neither is land with a rendering of a data center. Neither is a power allocation without a delivery date. Neither is fiber “nearby” if the workload requires paths, latency, and resilience that no one has verified. These are different commitments, made by different companies, on different timelines. Yet we often add them together and call the result capacity. That is a costly assumption. Before an AI site can serve a customer, someone has to establish where power will arrive, which networks can actually reach it, how the workload will perform, whether it can operate under local and sovereign requirements, and what it will cost to put the whole system into service. The gap between announced capacity and deployable capacity is where the next generation of infrastructure work begins. I call it The Infrastructure of Intelligence. At Connectbase, our work starts with Location Truth and Path Truth: knowing precisely where an opportunity exists, which routes can serve it, and how buyers, sellers, and partners can turn that knowledge into a transaction. It is central to our mission to build the Operating System for Ecosystem Connected Commerce. In this series, I’ll examine the physical, economic, and community decisions behind AI’s expansion—from programmable proximity and data center development to sovereign paths, trusted commerce, and physical AI. But first, I want to hear from the people building and buying this infrastructure: What should count as proof that announced AI capacity is actually deployable? small-business-owners-faced-cashflow-cri.text: Small Business Owners - Faced Cash-Flow Crisis & Budgeted Growth | Journo Request Sourcee Open main menu Features Pricing Reviews FAQ Log in Start free trial Posted in last 7 days Small Business Owners - Faced Cash-Flow Crisis & Budgeted Growth In 2019, only 23% of American households prepared a monthly budget. Families living paycheck to paycheck hit 74%. Think there’s a correlation? Most people would rather be poked in the eye with a sharp stick than hear the word “budget.” It sounds like giving something up. “Eat rice and beans forever.” It doesn’t have to be that way. True budgeting should be freeing — not constricting. A budget is simply money coming in minus money going out. Surplus or deficit. That’s it. Looking at spending can be upsetting, depressing, frightening. It just sucks sometimes. But if you want to CHANGE your financial future FOREVER, it must be done. Your check register is not a budget. Your banking app is not a budget. Do you have a real monthly account of where every dollar goes? Owner conversations start in the same place — a clear picture of money in and money out. No picture, no honest next chapter on growth or funding. On The Second Round, powered by Stacking Capital, we talk with people who finally faced the numbers in a hard season. Could you explain your cash flow the way you’d explain a household budget? We want to hear your story and share it — how you got started, how you funded it. No gimmicks, no fluff. Just the good, the bad, and the ugly. Want The Chair to share your story? Leave a comment below.
